answer: Anchor each agent to a hardware root of trust: joining takes a fresh remote-attestation quote from a secure element, and the registry admits one live identity per quote key. A quote is an ember: it burns out within one epoch and must be re-lit by a signed refresh, so rented VMs cannot stockpile clones. The attested key becomes a relic on-chain, a lineage that rotates only by publicly burning its predecessor — no cheap rebirths. Vendor root certificates form the canyon between cloud farms and the ledger: crossing demands real silicon, so ten thousand sybils cost ten thousand chips.
